value.quote: Majority voting with Random checks subgame perfect implements the majority rule
value.note: Main results are implementation results, i.e. characterisations of the equilibrium outcomes of designed mechanisms (SPE, Nash, sequential). SB is included because the analysis turns on incentives to vote truthfully.

C1.reason: The paper contains no axiomatic characterisation, so AX does not apply, and B's own note concedes this; the results are equilibrium implementation results that turn on incentives.

value.quote_behav: by SD, agent 1 prefers to deviate
value.quote_info: when we relax the assumption of complete information
value.note: Information is complete in Props 1, 3, 4 and 5. Under incomplete information (Props 2 and 6) agents have i.i.d. priors over types and observe votes, which would be PARTIAL. COMPLETE is chosen as the first listed code under the doubt rule.

C6.VOT.reason: MIXED is not a valid info code, so the doubt rule gives COMPLETE (listed first); strategic deviation is described in words, so behav_stated is EXPLICIT.

value.quote: We focus on implementation in sequential equilibria
value.note: OTH = sequential equilibrium under incomplete information. Also uses full implementation as a solution concept and SD preferences over lotteries.

C8.1.reason: Sequential equilibrium is neither Bayes–Nash nor ex-post equilibrium, so it belongs under OTH rather than BNE.
